files.asset_inspection: 1528x1749 RGBA PNG, transparent background. It is the light-appearance 'mascot' droplet layer of the Icon Composer bundle DroppyCode/Resources/AppIcon.icon (referenced by icon.json as layer name 'mascot ', image-name 'mascot (3).png', glass-specialization true for default/light, opacity 0 for dark and tinted appearances, position scale 0.5 / translation (0,36)). Visually: a single teardrop-shaped droplet with two oval white 'eyes' punched out near its base, rendered with soft internal shading (a bright highlight on the upper-left lobe, a darker gradient toward the lower-right) so it reads as a glossy/glass droplet mascot, surrounded by a soft white outer glow/halo. Between B2 and B3 the file's byte size changed from 614192 to 592376 bytes (git diff confirms a binary content change, 0 text lines by construction) with no dimension change; the droplet's fill color shifted from a lighter cyan-blue tone toward a more violet/periwinkle 'ultramarine' blue, matching the CHANGELOG.md B3 entry 'The app icon, the Droppy logo in Settings and the website's icons wear Droppy's new ultramarine blue' and the companion edit to DroppyCode/Resources/AppIcon.icon/icon.json's default fill-specialization linear-gradient, which moved from display-p3:0.56863,0.76863,1.00000 / srgb:0.14510,0.50196,1.00000 to srgb:0.51765,0.52549,0.96471 / srgb:0.07059,0.09804,0.92941.
files.purpose: This is the primary glossy droplet artwork Xcode's Icon Composer composites (together with shadow def.png, mascot dark.png, shadow dark.png and SVG Image.svg, per icon.json) into the macOS app icon shown for the light appearance. It exists purely as a build-time input to Xcode's icon compiler; no Swift source references it by name, and it produces pixels the OS renders, not a runtime-loaded asset.
platform_assumptions: Consumed only by Xcode's Icon Composer / actool at build time to emit the compiled .icns/AppIcon; there is no Windows equivalent build step for a .icon bundle, and ico/png icon generation on Windows follows an entirely different toolchain.
feature_notes: B2->B3 change is a pure recolor (new 'ultramarine' art-style blue per CHANGELOG.md and the paired icon.json gradient edit); geometry, layer role, opacity/glass specializations and every non-pixel property in icon.json for this layer are unchanged.

No requirement or UI record in porting/spec/*.json cites this file or 'AppIcon.icon' or 'mascot' at all (grep for the literal path, 'AppIcon.icon' and 'mascot' across every spec/*.json returned zero matches), so no record needs recite_lines_only / reclassify_behaviour_changed / retire_behaviour_removed treatment for this bundle.

Owner ruling OD-0002 makes the Windows app icon follow the separate 'Marrow' product identity, not Droppy's icon art, as an owner-approved parity deviation; the C# port (src/Marrow.App/Assets/icon.ico, icon.png, icon.svg, icon-mono.svg, icon-small.svg) already carries a bespoke Marrow icon unrelated to this file's pixels, and no unit in porting/deps/units.json maps a swift source to any target consuming 'mascot (3).png'. This B3 recolor therefore has no C# port impact under the current ruling; it is recorded here only because the file is in-scope for Gate A reading.

platform_assumptions: SwiftUI's Image("droppy-logo") resolves this through the Assets.xcassets catalog and its 1x/2x Contents.json; the Windows port instead ships plain PNG files loaded by path/resource id (src/Marrow.UI/Assets/Images/droppy-logo.png, droppy-logo@2x.png), with no catalog-driven scale selection.

grep -n "droppy-logo" across porting/spec/*.json finds three records that describe the image by its SwiftUI asset name rather than its file path: PR-SETTINGS-248 and PR-UPDATE-086 (both citing SettingsView.swift:1083-112[4/5] MadeByDroppyRow, 'a Link holding the \"droppy-logo\" image at 40 x 40') and UI-UPDATE-026 (colors field: 'the logo asset is \"droppy-logo\" at interpolation .high'). None of the three literally cite this file's path, and their cited line ranges are entirely inside SettingsView.swift, which is not part of this bundle and was not touched by this recolor, so their cited lines are untouched and unshifted -> recite_lines_only / no entry needed; none of the three hardcodes a specific color value that the recolor would falsify.

The actual image bytes the port ships, src/Marrow.UI/Assets/Images/droppy-logo.png, are sha256 0f5d9663a0d23c458ab8e2783237596e5618d482f4ac23f00ead91eccef04388 and 51677 bytes -- byte-for-byte the B2 (1.6.2) source image, confirmed against E:\Droppy\reference\droppy-code-v1.6.2\...\droppy-logo.png.
